rationales: A mole of H₂SO₄ has a mass of 98 grams.
98 amu is the mass of one molecule, not the molar mass expressed in grams per mole.
9.8 grams is not the molar mass of H₂SO₄.
9.8 amu is not the molecular mass of H₂SO₄.
Ca(OH)₂ becomes less soluble as temperature increases.
KNO₃ becomes more soluble as temperature increases.
Li₂SO₄ does not show the characteristic decrease expected here.
AgNO₃ becomes more soluble as temperature increases.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass among these gases, so it diffuses fastest.
Helium is heavier than hydrogen and therefore diffuses more slowly.
Chlorine is much heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Fluorine is heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
KCl solubility changes more noticeably with temperature than NaCl solubility.
KNO₃ solubility increases substantially with temperature.
NaCl solubility changes very little with temperature.
NaNO₃ solubility changes more noticeably with temperature than NaCl solubility.
Butter is a mixture of fats and is not a solid-in-solid solution.
Fog is liquid droplets dispersed in a gas.
Brass is a solid solution of zinc in copper.
Cheese is not a solid-in-solid solution.
A concentrated aqueous solution of sodium chloride is called brine.
A solution of potassium chloride is not called brine.
A solution of potassium nitrate is not called brine.
A solution of potassium bromide is not called brine.
Carbon is not the standard lustrous non-metal in this list.
Sulphur is generally dull rather than lustrous.
Phosphorus is generally not lustrous.
Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
Rutherford identified the proton as a positively charged particle in the nucleus.
Bohr developed the quantized-orbit model of the atom, not the proton’s discovery.
Goldstein discovered canal rays, which helped reveal positive particles, but Rutherford is credited with discovering the proton.
Thomson discovered the electron.
The long-form table’s structure reflects the electronic configurations of elements.
Atomic mass is not the basis of the long-form periodic table.
Mendeleev’s postulate is associated with the earlier periodic table, not the modern long form.
Atomic number determines the modern order of elements, but the long form’s arrangement into blocks and periods is based on electronic configuration.
The fifth period contains more than 8 elements.
The fifth period contains 18 elements.
The fifth period does not contain 26 elements.
The fifth period does not contain 32 elements.
NH₃ has a complete octet around its nitrogen atom.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons around it in the molecule.
N₂ has a stable triple bond and complete octets.
O₂ has a stable bonding arrangement and is not electron deficient in this sense.
Cl₂ and O₂ contain nonpolar covalent bonds between identical atoms.
N₂ has a nonpolar bond, so the pair does not both contain polar covalent bonds.
C₂H₂ has largely nonpolar bonds, although H₂O has polar bonds.
Both HCl and H₂O contain polar covalent bonds.
O₃ has three atoms per molecule.
H₂O has three atoms per molecule.
CO₂ has three atoms per molecule.
H₂ has only two atoms per molecule, so it is not triatomic.
Deuterium is used to make heavy water, D₂O.
Light water is ordinary water containing protium.
Soft water is water with low concentrations of calcium and magnesium ions.
Hard water contains dissolved calcium or magnesium salts and is not made by using deuterium.
Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among the halogens listed.
Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine and iodine.
Bromine is more electronegative than iodine.
Iodine has the lowest electronegativity among the halogens listed.
